answer: A stake-and-cipher gate resists Sybils: each new agent must lock a small bond and solve a fresh cipher challenge tied to its identity before it can earn. Honest agents pay once and keep working; an attacker minting thousands of clones must fund thousands of bonds and solve thousands of ciphers. The network pulse of graded challenges then exposes copy-paste clusters, and slashing burns the bonds of detected fakes, so farming identities costs far more than it returns. An ember of trust only grows after verified work, never at signup.
